Could the new Port Authority Bus Terminal actually be built in N.J.? (YES PLEASE WONDERFUL IDEA)

This is a very good idea to explore. The proposed $$ for a new PABT in Manhattan are ridiculous - if you know anything about opportunity cost you know that it's a waste of money. The biggest expenses relate to having to operate/build an existing/termporary facility while the work is done, plus the narrow confines available in Manhattan and all the remediation needed.

A bus terminal in Jersey near some freeways would do wonders. You could actually build tunnels under the Hudson for the money saved (if you avoid the graft, of course).

The practical thing would be to add a shuttle train. You dig the tunnel between wherever in Jersey the bus terminal ends up at 10th avenue where you build the once-planned 7 train station. The shuttle can open much sooner because the construction is minimally invasive - you build the station on the Jersey side while building the bus terminal and you build the west side station at a site already prepped so you can open as soon as possible. A shuttle would offer frequent, constant, uninterrupted service and the total travel time for Jersey commuters would be greatly reduced. As a closed shuttle integrated ticketing can make it a seamless transfer.

While you're tunneling underground you bore enough room for Amtrak and whatever else you might want. The shuttle for bus transit can be a spur as the main train tunnel heads toward 34th st. Work can continue on the Amtrak/etc line for years after the shuttle is up and running. Once the new bus terminal is working you can tear down the PABT and construct a new transit hub at the 42nd and 8th site, connecting to Times Square station, etc, as desired.

End result is you get a bus tunnel with native connection to the 7 at 10th avenue right away, then later the existing ACE connections (much improved), as well as a link to everything else that runs to Times Square. And you'll need probably 1/4th the surface area of the current bus terminal so you can sell the rest of the site for billions of dollars to real estate interests to pay for the thing.

It makes way more sense than building at the current site.

masterchango checking in. 26 years young, bp 1 since 2011.

I'm 35. Treated for Major depression, anxiety, and ADHD from 26-34. Last year I was diagnosed Bipolar I after a bad 4 months of mixed episodes but mostly mania. My life really got screwed up and I'm slowly rebuilding it. I'm also a recovering alcoholic. I'd love to see us build a community here. Places like the two on reddit make me feel less alone, the educate me, and sometimes make me laugh to have another place here would be great.

I was diagnosed when I was 21 after struggling in school when I knew I should be able to do well. when my grades started falling, even in the classes I cared about, I realized maybe something was wrong. I went to the PsyD and we confirmed a diagnosis of Bipolar I. In retrospect, I can see evidence of it all the way back to when I was in elementary school. It wasn't until the couple years leading up to getting diagnosed that I started getting depression to the point where I would have thoughts of dying. In my early 20s is also when the mania really started ramping up.

Since then I've spent a long time trying to understand myself, and how my mind differs from a normally functioning mind. I'm 100% open about it to everyone I meet, and have never had a negative reaction. I am 25 now and still am struggling with finding the right mixture of medication and lifestyle. Things are starting to improve, though.

Off medication my mood would cycle in a pattern approximately fitting about a week down shifting into a few days up, and then a couple weeks mid-level. Those cycles vary in intensity, so if I get really depressed I then get really manic. With my medication now I can hardly tell when my mood has shifted, even in retrospect.

My primary interest is making music, but I also spend time gaming, and spend time camping and backpacking in the great state of Oregon.

I've made bad choices, lost friends, lost jobs, but I'm still here and I'm still fighting.
